My extra Gowans API searches (stove, 1950s stove, metters, kooka, electric range, vintage oven, retro oven, enamel, cooker, xcel stove, enamel stove, vintage stove, retro stove) found no past vintage enamel kitchen stove, only camp and gas stoves. WebSearch was refused (budget used up), so Armitage past results, dealer listings and interstate auction houses were not checked. A follow-up with more search budget could check those.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: oval chrome badge on the oven door (four letters, consistent with XCEL but not readable), small enamel plaque low on the door panel (not legible), timer dial and three knobs on a cream panel, one black knob by the door latch. Photo 2: oven open, enamel liner grimy with rust on the lower edges, two racks present. Photo 3: top compartment flap open. The flap has a tear or split at the centre of its lower edge, the grill area is dirty and there is a loose tray inside. Photo 4: both coil plates are present and look complete. The solid plate is heavily crusted with burnt residue or corrosion, and there are small chips on the green top. Splashback brackets are intact. Legs and side panels look sound with general wear.
lots.condition: Used and untested. Oven and grill compartments are dirty with surface rust. The solid hotplate is heavily crusted. Enamel chips on the cooktop. Tear or dent in the drop-down flap. Treat the original wiring from about 1950 as unsafe until an electrician has checked it. A stove like this needs a hard-wired 240V circuit, not a plug.
lots.question_for_armitage: Can you read the maker's badge and any rating plate (maker, model, voltage, wattage, country)? Has it been tested or powered up, and is the original wiring and flex intact? Do all elements, the timer and the switches work, and are the oven racks and grill tray complete? How bad is the damage to the drop-down flap, and is there any rust-through on the base or back?
lots.score_reason: A complete-looking 1950s enamel stove in a popular green and cream finish has some appeal to retro kitchen, film prop and shack or glamping buyers. Against that, it is bulky, untested and grimy, has a damaged flap and a crusted plate, and I found no sale evidence at any price. My guess is a modest $30 to $150, marked down because there is no evidence.
